RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 55

An all-male panel is a recognized risk factor for implicit bias and homophily, and it may violate university regulations requiring gender diversity on hiring committees. Given your stronger traditional metrics (completed PhD, more publications, extensive teaching), gender bias is plausible, though the panel may genuinely have prioritized specific industry ties or subfield fit for this lectureship. 

Do not accuse them of discrimination directly without proof, as this carries career risks. First, send a polite follow-up requesting your feedback. Simultaneously, check university and union policies regarding search committee composition. If an all-male panel breached procedural rules, raise that procedural failure—ideally through a union or faculty ombudsperson—rather than lodging an unsubstantiated bias claim.
